key_insight: In a retrospective simulation, Sybil identified 33.8% of negative lung cancer screens for biennial rather than annual screening, with no delayed cancer diagnoses observed.
clinical_relevance: AI-guided screening intervals could reduce follow-up imaging workload and expand screening capacity, but prospective validation is needed before clinical adoption.
method: Analyzed 3,120 lung cancer screens from a tertiary safety-net hospital.
Externally evaluated Sybil, focusing on low-risk Lung-RADS 1/2 screens.
Simulated interval extension using Sybil and Brock risk scores calibrated on an NLST subset.
evidence_signal: Sybil's 2-year AUC was 0.746 for Lung-RADS 1/2 screens; the cohort had 72 cancers and a median follow-up of 2.3 years.
watch_item: The single-center, retrospective simulation does not establish the safety of biennial screening in prospective practice.
paper_title: Investigating AI's potential in risk-stratifying lung cancer screenings for extending screening intervals and reducing workload: A retrospective analysis of a tertiary hospital cohort
